qa.question: What year did CT4 at Marshall reach mothballed status?
qa.finding: I found no TVA board action, plan or filing that dates a mothballing of CT4. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists CT4 with status standby, available for service but not normally used, and an operating date in 2002. The 2026 TVA integrated resource plan, volume 2 (https://tva-azr-eastus-cdn-ep-tvawcm-prd.azureedge.net/cdn-tvawcma/docs/default-source/environment/environmental-stewardship/integrated-resource-plan/2026-irp/prelimfinal-2026-irp-vol-2-eis_20260618_r1.pdf?sfvrsn=208e1a89_3), lists Marshall as an existing plant of 8 units with no retirement or new unit.
qa.recommendation: Leave the mothball date blank and add no retired year. Ask TVA for the date if the database needs one.
qa.note: I searched the EIA table, the TVA 2026 integrated resource plan volumes 1 and 2, the Kentucky air permit from February 2023 and a web search. The TVA plan page is at https://www.tva.com/environment/2026-integrated-resource-plan. TVA is outside Kentucky Public Service Commission jurisdiction, and no commission case matched. In the third pass I also read the TVA Marshall plant page at https://www.tva.com/energy/our-power-system/natural-gas/marshall-combustion-turbine-plant and a January 2018 WCBL article at https://www.marshallcountydaily.com/2018/01/10/combustion-turbine-plant-keeps-tva-power-going-strong/. Neither says when any unit was mothballed. A web search for the mothballing date also found nothing from TVA. Board minutes were not searched.
